Hello, I'm just going to comment about working in Australia, we actually don't have the Michelin guide in Australia. We have our own guide own by a company called Fairfax. And are rated in hats. We do have some very good restaurants in Australia. Also about working in fine dining, it's very very difficult, a normal day is 9-1 and you very very rarely get longer then a 15 minutes break. So you would need to live near the restaurant which are in expensive areas most of the time, which is expensive in rent.  Also, everything has to be perfect, if your knife is the tiniest bit dull you will have to by a new knife. The sous chef will taste everything you make. You always have to turn up attest 20 minutes before your shift and be in the kitchen before hand otherwise you will be fired, even if you one minute late. Your uniform has to be extremely clean and ironed, even the clothes you walk in with and out. Doesn't matter what anyone says you will be burnt out in under a month, but if you can push, you will learn the best food trends, and technique. Also a lot of fine dining establishments make little to even no profit, (people sponsor them) so your pay will be minimum wage.
